CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit status post mitral valve repair.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Melissa Sanchez is a patient who underwent mitral valve repair on 8/3/2020. She was seen at previous follow-up on 9/17 and was doing well from a cardiac standpoint. She reports overall improvement compared to her condition prior to surgery. She continues to experience occasional chest pain and shallow breathing with exertion, occurring a few times per month. Each episode lasts only a few minutes and is followed by a symptom-free period of several weeks. She has learned to manage symptoms by reducing exertion when they occur, which allows her to resume and complete activities after resting. She denies new symptoms. She reports good medication compliance using a reminder app. Past medical history includes mitral regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, asthma, and recurrent chest discomfort with prior negative workup for coronary artery disease.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports exertional chest pain and exertional dyspnea that resolve with rest. She denies palpitations or other cardiac symptoms. She initially experienced irritability from atenolol but has adjusted to this side effect. She denies other medication side effects.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Mitral valve repair (8/3/2020)
- Mitral regurgitation
- Atrial fibrillation
- Diabetes
- Asthma
- Chest discomfort with negative cardiac workup for coronary artery disease

MEDICATIONS
- Coumadin 4 mg daily
- Lasix 4 mg daily
- Atenolol 50 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not documented.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well.
Head and Neck: No jugular venous distension detected.
Lungs: Reduced breath sounds, but auscultation and percussion are clear.
Heart: Irregularly irregular rhythm, S1 slightly accentuated, no S3 gallop.
Abdomen: Non-tender to palpation.
Extremities: Trace peripheral edema, non-tender.

RESULTS
Electrocardiogram (12/26/2020): Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response, T-wave inversion anteriorly. No significant changes compared to previous study.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Status post mitral valve repair - Patient recovering well. Heart valves functioning well.
2. Atrial fibrillation - Well controlled on current medical therapy. Continue Coumadin 4 mg daily, Lasix 4 mg daily, and Atenolol 50 mg daily.
3. Exertional chest pain and dyspnea - Manageable with activity modification. Encourage continued activity as tolerated.
4. Follow-up in 6-9 months.
